description: We are a team of students from TED Rönesans College, eager to explore the mysteries of space. We study the stories of spacecraft that have explored the Moon, Mars, and deep space, and their contributions to science. We love researching, asking questions, and developing new ideas. We are excited to join the NASA Space Apps Challenge to explore the history of space exploration and carry its scientific legacy into the future!
summary: When a spacecraft goes silent, what can it still teach us? In Goodnight, Space: Duru’s First Broadcast, we built a story-driven browser game for young explorers. During her first show on Moon Base Radio, Duru follows the trail of 15 NASA missions across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Players fly to the hardware, make engineering choices, and hear the stories behind its discoveries. By turning real challenges, such as flying in Mars’s thin atmosphere or spotting a planet in a brief dip in starlight, into moments of play, our game answers the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge. We want children to see that a mission can end while the science it made possible continues to teach us.
details:
“When your mission ended, what did you leave behind?” Duru asks this question on her first Moon Base Radio broadcast. When no one answers over the radio, she follows the traces of NASA missions across 15 stops on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space. Eagle’s descent stage, left on the Moon, tells the story of how the astronauts began their journey home. Spirit’s broken wheel uncovers an unexpected clue about water on Mars. By the end of the broadcast, these pieces come together: the machines have gone quiet, but the data they left behind still tells a story.

Technology Stack

We built the browser game with HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript, using Canvas for flight scenes and browser audio for narration and sound effects. We kept the keyboard and touch controls simple so players can focus on the story. The current version offers English narration and on-screen text. We used ElevenLabs for the English dub with Duru’s permission, OpenAI Image Generation for the final pixel art, Gemini for early visual drafts, and ChatGPT to assist with development and script editing.

Innovation Highlights

  • Gameplay leads players into the story. At most stops, three stars reveal the spacecraft. Players reach it and answer an engineering question before unlocking Duru’s account.
  • Players try a version of the science themselves. At the Kepler stop, they record a planetary transit by responding to a dip in a star’s brightness. They try the method before Duru explains it.
  • The broadcast is fictional; the mission data is real. Mission cards link to NASA sources. The Ingenuity card, for example, shows that its first flight reached 3 meters and lasted 39.1 seconds, with a link to NASA’s flight log.

How to play: Download and extract the entire ZIP, then open index.html in your browser and click Start Broadcast.
